column4: ### Defining Faith
column5: ### Definition of Faith

column4: Faith is a commonly misunderstood and misrepresented aspect of Christianity. As the saying goes, “there is a ditch on both sides of the road”! Because the word faith is so commonly used without proper explanation in our modern Christianity, it can come to pick up erroneous definitions amplified through misunderstanding. Faith is often portrayed either as a blanketed statement of abstracted belief or as an almost mystical power or “magic,” something you possess in a specific measured and limited amount.
column5: Faith is an aspect of Christianity that is often misunderstood and misrepresented. As the proverb says, "There is a ditch on both sides of the road"! In modern Christianity, the word faith is used so commonly without adequate explanation that it can come to carry mistaken definitions amplified by misunderstandings. Faith is often portrayed either as a sweeping statement of abstracted belief or as an almost mystical power, that is, "magic," something one possesses only in a certain measured, limited amount.

column4: #### What Faith is Not
column5: #### What Faith Is Not

column4: Faith misrepresented abstractly has no specific conviction or persuasion. This is often evident with a bit of probing as this representation of faith cannot be made specific. If you ask, ‘what do you believe’ or ‘why do you believe’ the person with this understanding of faith often cannot clarify beyond ‘I believe’. 1 Peter 3:15 says we should be ready to give an answer for the hope that is in us.
column5: When faith is misrepresented in an abstract way, there is no concrete conviction or persuasion. This becomes clear when you probe a little, because such expressions of faith cannot be made concrete. When asked "What do you believe?" or "Why do you believe?", those who hold this understanding often cannot clarify beyond "I believe." 1 Peter 3:15 says that we should be ready to give a defense for the hope that is in us.

column4: Sometimes people think of faith like a magical power-but that’s not what Scripture teaches. Faith is about a real relationship built on trust. In Scripture, faith is far more dynamic and relational-it’s rooted in persuasion, trust, and confidence in God’s character and promises. It’s not an impersonal force but an engaged response to God that shapes thoughts, feelings, and actions.
column5: At times people think of faith as a magical power - but that is not what the Bible teaches. Faith involves a real relationship built on trust. In Scripture, faith is far more dynamic and relational - it is rooted in assurance, trust, and confidence in God's character and promises. It is not an impersonal force, but a volitional response to God that shapes thoughts, feelings, and actions.

column4: #### Faith is Persuasion
column5: #### Faith Is Conviction

column4: So, what is faith? Persuasion! The Greek word ***pistis*** means persuasion, or the result of being persuaded. We are to have persuasion towards God. In English we might say faith (persuasion) ‘**in** God’. If you are married, you hopefully have faith ‘**in’** your spouse. You believe that they will do what they said they would do, and you believe that they are being authentic and genuine. This trust should extend beyond what they’ve said, to extend to them in general.
column5: Then, what is faith? Assurance! The Greek ***pistis*** means assurance, or the result obtained by being persuaded. We are asked to have assurance toward God. In English, we might express faith (assurance) as ‘**in** God’. If you are married, hopefully you trust your spouse. That is, you believe your spouse ‘**in’**. You believe your spouse will do what they said, and that the person is faithful and genuine. This trust should extend beyond their words to the whole person.

column4: Developing faith, persuasion, and trust in a relationship takes time and experience. Hopefully in life you have learned how to develop a trusting relationship with another person. The principles you’ve learned that allow you to increase your trust in someone you know will also allow you can increase your faith in God. Faith in a relationship is increased over time, in experience, with consistency, and through small and large actions that build your confidence in the other person’s character and nature.
column5: It takes time and experience to cultivate faith, assurance, and trust in relationships. Hopefully, you have learned how to build trust with others in your life. The principles you have learned to increase your trust in someone you know also help to increase your faith in God. Faith in a relationship is increased through time and experience, consistency, and through actions—from small to large—that build confidence in the other’s character and nature.

column4: ‘Faith towards God’, is relational. Relationships are built by two parties, not one. The good news about our faith in God is that God is responsible for His side of the relationship (made possible by the atoning death of Jesus, and the infilling of His spirit at rebirth), and He helps us on our side too (through the work of the Comforter - the Holy Spirit). God is doing almost all the work, our part (as we will discuss later in this chapter) is to walk *WITH* Him in obedience.

column4: ### Jesus Matures Our Faith
column5: ### Jesus matures our faith

column4: Jesus is the author and perfecter of our faith (Hebrews 12:2). Our faith is designed to be continually growing and expanding. We don’t reach a single point where we have enough ‘faith’, but rather our faith increases. Consider a deep and personal relationship you have in your life today. As in any relationship we don't arrive at a specific milestone where now we ‘know’ the person. We continue to know them, and increase our knowledge of them, and this refines, shapes, and grows our relationship.
column5: Jesus is the author and finisher of our faith (Hebrews 12:2)。 Our faith is intended to constantly grow and expand。 We do not reach a single point and obtain “enough ‘faith,’” but rather faith keeps increasing。 Think now of a deep, personal relationship in your life。 In any relationship, you do not arrive at a point where you have “come to ‘know’ that person.” We continue to know that person, deepen our understanding of them, and that refines, shapes, and grows the relationship。

column4: How do we grow our faith in God? By continuing to experience Him across His many revelations, manifestations, and attributes. Again, consider a deep personal relationship in your life. You increase the depth of relationship by engaging them in different ways, in different formats, in different mediums, in different settings. You talk to them, message them, perhaps write to them. You see them individually, and in group settings. You talk about what you value, and perhaps you challenge one another. The numerous ways go on to infinity. Across these many expressions you come to know the person more deeply.
column5: How do we grow in faith toward God? column4: There are two Greek words for ‘Word’ in the Bible-**logos** and **rhema**. Understanding the difference helps us see how faith grows.
column5: In the Bible, there are two Greek words for 「word」—**logos** and **rhema**。 By understanding this difference, we can see how faith grows。

column4: **Logos**: generally, refers to the **concept, idea, reason, or broader expression of God’s word**. It encompasses a universal, foundational truth or message and is often used to describe God’s eternal wisdom and Christ Himself as the living Word.
column5: **Logos**: Generally refers to the concept, thought, reason, or broader expression of the word of God。 It encompasses universal and foundational truths or messages and is often used to represent God’s eternal wisdom and Christ Himself, the living Word。

column4: **Rhema (G4487)**: emphasizes a **specific, spoken word or utterance**. It typically refers to a particular word or message given in a specific moment, especially a spoken or revealed word that applies directly to a person’s situation.
column5: **Rhema（G4487）**：emphasizes a **specific, spoken word or utterance**. Typically, it refers to a special word or message given at a particular moment, especially a spoken or revealed word that applies directly to a person's situation.

column4: *Logos* is like the entire message of a book, whereas *rhema* is like a particular passage or sentence that speaks directly to someone at a given moment. While *logos* is God’s overarching truth, *rhema* is when part of that truth is spoken to an individual in a personal, applicable way. Together, they illustrate the fullness of God’s communication: *logos* as the broad, foundational truths of God’s character and will, and *rhema* as the specific, applied word that brings that truth alive in a person’s life and situation.
column5: *Logos* is like the message of an entire book, and *Rhema* is like a specific passage or sentence that speaks directly to a person at that time. While *Logos* is God’s comprehensive truth, *Rhema* is that a portion of that truth is spoken to an individual in a personal and applicable way. Both show the fullness of God’s communication; that is, *Logos* is the broad, foundational truth of God’s nature and will, and *Rhema* is the concrete, applied word that makes that truth come alive within a person’s life and circumstances.

column4: ### Example of a Rhema Word in Action
column5: ### An example of how a Rhema word works

column4: God promises revelation and wisdom for all those that ask. When He speaks to us, that utterance is a *rhema* word. Rhema words are from God and serve to confirm, lead, and guide us. They are not a replacement for the *logos* word, nor do they carry authority of scripture. *Rhema* words are to be judged by the same standard as prophecy or interpretation of tongues (see the chapter on the Holy Spirit for an in-depth study on this topic).
column5: God promises revelation and wisdom to all who ask. When God speaks to us, that utterance is a *Rhema* word. A Rhema word is from God; it confirms, guides, and directs us. It is not a replacement for the *Logos* word, nor does it carry the authority of Scripture. A *Rhema* word should be tested by the same standards as prophecy and the interpretation of tongues（see the chapter on the Holy Spirit for a detailed study of this subject）.

column4: At several points in my career, I have prayed for divine guidance. Several years ago, I was contemplating the process of starting to look for a new opportunity and in my prayer time, I heard God say to me ‘*Just wait on me, I have an opportunity for you.’* I was starting to look for a new job because I was dissatisfied with my current role and felt frustrated. God’s word of direction ‘*wait on me’* helped me have peace and confidence in an otherwise restless season.
column5: Several times in my career, I prayed and sought God’s guidance. A few years ago, when I was wondering whether I should start looking for a new opportunity, I heard God say to me in prayer, 「‘*Just wait on me, I have an opportunity for you.’*」. I was dissatisfied with and frustrated by my role at the time, so I had started looking for a new job. Through God’s word of direction, 「‘*wait on me’*」, I was able to have peace and confidence even in a restless season.

column4: Three of four months passed, I kept working hard and faithfully, keeping my attitude positive. God would remind me, *‘wait on me’*, then His promise occurred. I had an opportunity to be promoted and received a generous wage increase.
column5: After three or four months passed, I continued to work hard and faithfully, maintaining a positive attitude. God often reminded me, 「*‘wait on me’*」, and eventually that promise was fulfilled. I received a promotion opportunity and a generous pay increase.

column4: I could have continued my job search; I could have left. I could have started somewhere new. No doubt someone else would have gotten that promotion! But because I sought the Lord’s counsel and was persuaded in His **rhema word**, I obeyed, and received the benefit. God’s words are **alive and personal**, and He promises to give us manifold and liberal wisdom (James 1:5).
column5: I could have continued job hunting, quit, or started somewhere new. Without a doubt, someone else would have gotten that promotion! However, because I sought the Lord’s counsel and gained confidence in that **Rhema word**, I obeyed and benefited. God’s word is **living and personal**, and He promises to give us much, abundant wisdom（James 1:5）。

column4: I have dozens if not hundreds of times where I have prayed and asked God what to do and He has given me a rhema word. Not each had the same spectacular outcome, but they all brought a sense of peace and confidence that I was obeying God and that He would work things out. They were the words I needed for the moment! column5: Dozens of times, indeed, hundreds, I have prayed and asked God what I should do, and God has given me a Rhema word. column4: Jesus goes on to say, ‘*blessed are they who have not seen and have believe*d’. This is not Jesus encouraging ‘blind or ignorant faith’ or rejecting the use of empirical evidence. But He is saying that we are more blessed when we can believe without the need for empirical proof. Why? If our faith, our trust, was limited to purely what we had seen empirically demonstrated, we could never have any confidence in the future work. We would have great confidence in what had been accomplished but would not walk in the peace of God for our tomorrows and for our future.
column5: Jesus further says, 「‘*blessed are they who have not seen and have believe*d’」. This is not Jesus encouraging 「‘blind and ignorant faith’」 or rejecting the use of empirical evidence. Rather, He is saying that we are more blessed when we can believe without requiring empirical proof. Why is that? If our faith—that is, our trust—were purely limited to only what has been empirically shown, we would have no assurance regarding future works. We might have great confidence in what has been accomplished in the past, but we would not be able to walk in God’s peace concerning tomorrow and the future.

column4: Beyond core relational skills, there are specific practices and disciplines that will strengthen your relationship with God:
column5: In addition to core relational skills, there are specific practices and training that strengthen your relationship with God.

column4: - **Build and Maintain a Prayer Life, Listen and Communicate with God.** Regular, heartfelt prayer is essential to a close relationship with God. Through prayer, you can share your worries, joys, and gratitude, seeking His guidance and strength. (*Philippians 4:6-7*) Being sensitive to the Holy Spirit’s voice helps you discern God’s will, find wisdom in decisions, and grow in spiritual maturity. Take time for quiet reflection to hear His direction. (*Romans 8:14*)
column5: - **Build and maintain a life of prayer, listening to God and conversing with Him.** Regular, heartfelt prayer is indispensable to an intimate relationship with God. Through prayer, you can share your anxieties, joys, and gratitude, and seek God's guidance and strength. (*Philippians 4:6-7*) Being sensitive to the voice of the Holy Spirit helps you discern God's will, gain wisdom in decisions, and grow toward spiritual maturity. Take time to quietly reflect and listen for God's guidance. (*Romans 8:14*)

column4: - **Spend Time in Worship.** Worship is a powerful way to draw close to God, expressing love and reverence. Through praise, song, or quiet reflection, worship deepens your awareness of His presence. (*Psalms 100:2-4*)
column5: - **Have times of worship.** Worship is a powerful way to draw near to God while expressing love and reverence. Through praise, song, and quiet contemplation, worship deepens your awareness of God's presence. (*Psalm 100:2-4*)

column4: - **Read, Study, and Meditate on Scripture.** God’s Word reveals His character, promises, and instructions for life. Dedicating time to studying Scripture helps you grow in faith, understanding, and spiritual resilience. (*2 Timothy 3:16-17*)
column5: - **Read, study, and meditate on the Bible.** God's word reveals His character, promises, and guidance for life. Devoting time to study the Scriptures helps grow faith, understanding, and spiritual resilience. (*2 Timothy 3:16-17*)

column4: - **Obey His Commandments.** Obedience to God’s instructions demonstrates your love, respect, and trust in Him. Walking in obedience aligns your life with His purpose and brings blessings. (*John 14:15*)
column5: - **Obey God's commandments.** Obeying God's instructions shows love, reverence, and trust for God. Walking in obedience aligns your life with God's purposes and brings blessing. (*John 14:15*)

column4: - **Actively Attend a Local Church and Serve.** Engaging in a church community offers spiritual support, encouragement, and opportunities to serve others. Being involved helps build a sense of belonging and strengthens your commitment to God’s mission. (*Hebrews 10:24-25*)
column5: - **Gather with and serve actively in a local church.** Involvement in a church community provides spiritual support and encouragement and offers opportunities to serve others. By engaging, a sense of belonging is nurtured and your commitment to God's mission is strengthened. (*Hebrews 10:24-25*)

column4: - **Build Relationships with Other Believers.** Fellowship with other Christians provides accountability, encouragement, and shared wisdom. These relationships enrich your faith journey and help you grow through mutual support. (*Proverbs 27:17*)
column5: - **Build relationships with other believers.** Fellowship with other Christians brings accountability, encouragement, and shared wisdom. These relationships enrich your journey of faith and help you grow through mutual support. (*Proverbs 27:17*)

column4: Our ‘faith towards God’ is not a one-time occurrence for salvation but is an ongoing practice and relationship that we are supposed to cultivate our entire lives. The benefits of a trusting and beneficial relationship are incredibly numerous, but we must do the good work of fostering that trust and growth to see it thrive.
column5: Our ‘faith in God’ is not a one-time event for salvation, but an ongoing practice and relationship to be cultivated throughout life. The benefits of a trusting, fruitful relationship are truly countless, but to see that relationship thrive powerfully, we must do the good work of nurturing that trust and growth.
